title: FlowConfig
description:
Top-level application configuration structure.

Loaded from `%USERPROFILE%\.config\flow\flow.toml` (see [`config::dirs`](crate::config::dirs)
for the full resolution chain including `--config` flag and `FLOW_CONFIG_DIR` env var
overrides). The struct carries `#[serde(default)]`, so the file may be partial or even empty —
serde fills missing fields from the [`Default`] impl.

The canonical default values live in the `Default` impl below. The `default-config.toml` file is
a hand-written **example** copied to users by `flow config init` — it is not read at runtime.

This struct contains **application settings only** — padding,
animation, etc. Window classification rules live in a separate file
([`WindowRulesConfig`]) to allow independent editing.

# Column Sizing

The primary column sizing mode is [`columns_per_screen`](FlowConfig::columns_per_screen):
the user specifies how many columns fit on one monitor, and the daemon computes
the actual pixel width at runtime from the monitor resolution and [`window_gap`](Padding::window_gap).

Power users can override this by setting [`column_width`](FlowConfig::column_width)
to a fixed pixel value. When `column_width` is `Some`, it takes priority over
`columns_per_screen` — the auto-computation is skipped entirely.

# Example

```toml
columns_per_screen = 4
min_column_width_px = 640

[padding]
window_gap = 16
up = 16
down = 16

[animation]
enabled = true
duration_ms = 240
easing = "ease-out-expo"
```

See `docs/spec/04-config-and-persistence.md` for the full schema.

adopt_maximized.description:
Whether a **maximized** window the daemon meets — in the startup
scan, when it opens, on `tiling on` — is un-maximized and classified
through the rules (tiled or floated as they say) instead of being
left alone as `Ignored(Maximized)`. Fullscreen windows (games,
videos) are never adopted, and neither is a window the rules
ignore. An adopted window is handed back maximized by `tiling off`,
`flow stop` and the fail-back. Off by default (upstream behaviour: a
maximized window is ignored until it is restored or `set-window` is
run on it, which adopts it either way). Live-reloadable.

check_for_updates.description:
Whether `flow start` runs the update checker (the same one behind
`flow update`, see [`UpdateConfig`]) and prints a one-line notice
when something newer exists on GitHub.

**Off by default in this fork**: a window manager has no business
phoning out at every start. The key is kept so a user can opt in.
When on, the check runs *after* the daemon is ready, is bounded by
a short network timeout, and silences all errors — it never blocks
or aborts startup, and it never downloads anything. The explicit
`flow update` command is unaffected by this flag. See
(`docs/src/dev-guide/updater.md`).

column_width.description:
Fixed column width in pixels — power-user override.

When `Some`, this overrides the auto-computation from [`columns_per_screen`](FlowConfig::columns_per_screen).
When `None`, the daemon computes the width from the monitor resolution, `columns_per_screen`,
and `window_gap`.

This field is **optional** in TOML — most users should rely on `columns_per_screen`.
A missing `Option` field deserializes to `None` automatically.

columns.description:
Column width presets (`[columns]`). `None` when the section is absent:
columns are then sized from [`columns_per_screen`](Self::columns_per_screen)
/ [`column_width`](Self::column_width) as before. When present, every
monitor starts on `columns.default` and `flow dispatch width` walks
the presets — see [`ColumnsConfig`].

columns_per_screen.description:
Number of columns that fit side-by-side on one monitor screen.

The daemon computes the actual pixel width at startup:
`base_content_width = (monitor_width - (N+1) * window_gap) / N`
where `N = columns_per_screen`.

If [`column_width`](FlowConfig::column_width) is also set, that value
takes priority and this field is ignored.

min_column_width_px.description: Minimum column width in pixels. Columns cannot be resized below this.

min_row_height_px.description:
Minimum row height in pixels — the dedicated vertical floor for
drag-resize of a single row (ticket #10). Mirrors
[`min_column_width_px`](Self::min_column_width_px) on the vertical axis:
dragging a row boundary cannot shrink either row below this value, and
once the shrinking neighbor hits it the edge elastically pins (overshoot
during the drag, snap back on release).

This is distinct from [`min_window_height_px`](Self::min_window_height_px),
which is the row-stack-count cap consulted by the add/remove/merge
mutations. The two are independent: a power user may want a higher
drag-floor than the stack cap, or vice versa. Both default to `100`.

min_window_height_px.description:
Minimum row height in pixels — the floor for any single window's
allocated height inside a column.

This bounds the maximum number of rows (windows) that can stack inside
one column: a column cannot grow rows beyond `available_height /
min_window_height_px`. It is also the lower clamp for future
drag-resize / IPC continuous-height adjustment of individual rows.

See (`docs/src/dev-guide/layout/mutations.md`) for the height-
distribution formula and the `merge-column` / `promote` operations.

minimize_restore.description: Behavior when a minimized tiling window is restored.

navigation.description: Navigation behaviour at the edges of a strip (`[navigation]`).

update.description:
What `flow update` (and the start-time notice) compares this build
against (`[update]`). See [`UpdateConfig`].

AnimationConfig.description:
Animation configuration for layout transitions.

When disabled, all window position changes are applied instantly
without animation.

easing.description:
Easing curve applied to window position channels (x, y).

See [`ConfigEasing`] for the full list of supported curves.
Defaults to [`ConfigEasing::EaseOutExpo`].

BorderConfig.description:
Window border overlay configuration.

The border crate draws a thin colored ring around each managed window as a
separate layered overlay window that follows the target HWND's geometry
(driven by `EVENT_OBJECT_LOCATIONCHANGE`). The daemon shrinks the actual
window rect by `(thickness - overlap)` pixels on each side so the colored
ring sits in the surrounding gap and overlaps the visible content by
`overlap` px (closing the DWM hairline gap). See
`docs/src/dev-guide/borders.md` for the full coordinate-space model.

# Example

```toml
[borders]
enabled = true
thickness = 3
overlap = 1
focused_color = "#00AAFF"
unfocused_color = "#555555"
floating_color = "#AA00FF"
```

enabled.description:
Master switch. When `false`, no overlay windows are created and any
existing overlays are detached.

focused_color.description: Border color for the focused/active window.

overlap.description:
How many pixels the border ring overlaps the window's visible content.

Komorebi-style overlap. `0` keeps the ring entirely in the reserved
gap (window shrinks by the full `thickness`); higher values pull the
content edge outward until, at `overlap == thickness`, the content
fills the whole layout slot and the ring sits fully on top of it. The
default of `1` closes the 1px DWM-client-edge hairline that otherwise
shows between an unfocused ring and the window content. Capped at
`thickness` by [`BorderConfig::validate`]. (`docs/src/dev-guide/borders.md`)

thickness.description:
Border ring thickness in pixels, applied uniformly on all four sides.

The ring is drawn in the outer `thickness` px of each window's layout
slot. The visible window content shrinks by `(thickness - overlap)` px
per edge (see `overlap`), so the ring overlaps the content by `overlap`
px rather than leaving a gap. (`docs/src/dev-guide/borders.md`)

ColumnsConfig.description:
The `[columns]` section: an ordered list of width presets and the one
every monitor starts on, plus optional per-screen rules. Absent from
`flow.toml` (`FlowConfig::columns` is `None`) the daemon sizes columns
from `columns_per_screen` / `column_width` exactly as before.

default.description:
The preset every monitor starts on. Must be one of `presets`; when
omitted the first preset is the default.

max_rows.description:
The most rows a column may hold; `0` (the default) is unlimited.
Merging into a full column moves the window past it instead. Must be
at least `visible_rows` when both are set.

presets.description:
Ordered presets; `flow dispatch width next|prev|cycle` walks this
list and wraps around. A preset is a fraction (`"1/2"`) or a pattern
(`"1/3+2/3"`).

screen.description:
`[[columns.screen]]`: screens matched by a rule use its list instead;
the first matching rule wins.

visible_rows.description:
How many rows of a stacked column are on screen at once. `0` (the
default) shows every row sharing the height, as before. With
`visible_rows = 2` a column of four windows shows two, and
`focus up/down` scrolls through the stack.

ConfigEasing.description:
Named easing curves available in user configuration.

Each variant corresponds to an easing function implemented in
[`crate::animation::easing::EasingStyle`]. The variant names use
CSS-like kebab-case when serialized to TOML (e.g. `EaseOutExpo` →
`"ease-out-expo"`).

The full set mirrors the 31 named curves in the animation engine.
`CubicBezier` is excluded because it requires four `f64` parameters
that cannot be expressed as a simple serde enum variant.

# Design Decision

This enum lives in the `config/` layer (not `animation/`) to honour
the module dependency hierarchy: `config/` may only import from
`common/`, never from `animation/`. The conversion from
`ConfigEasing` → `EasingStyle` is performed in the `daemon/` layer
(see [`crate::daemon::config_derive`]).

# Example

```toml
[animation]
easing = "ease-in-out-cubic"
```

DragConfig.description:
Tile-drag configuration.

Controls the behavior of drag-and-drop repositioning of tiled windows.
When a user drags a tiled window by its title bar, a live non-committing
preview reflows the other windows to the prospective layout on each zone
change; on release the move commits and the dragged window snaps into its
slot. Floating windows never enter the drag state machine. See
(`docs/src/dev-guide/tile-drag.md`).

# Example

```toml
[drag]
edge_scroll_width = 30
col_edge_ratio = 0.18
col_edge_max_px = 120
edge_scroll_initial_delay_ms = 500
edge_scroll_repeat_interval_ms = 240
```

col_edge_max_px.description:
Pixel cap on the column-insert hit band. The effective band is
`min(col_edge_ratio * column_width, col_edge_max_px)`.

edge_scroll_initial_delay_ms.description:
Edge-scroll auto-repeat **initial delay** in milliseconds — the gap
between the immediate scroll fired on entering the band and the first
repeat. Clamped up to the effective repeat interval at runtime, so `0`
cleanly means "glide at the normal cadence with no special pause."

edge_scroll_repeat_interval_ms.description:
Edge-scroll auto-repeat **repeat interval** in milliseconds — the gap
between successive column scrolls while the cursor is held in the band.
Clamped up to the enabled animation duration and the spam-guard floor at
runtime; a sub-floor value additionally logs a startup warning.

edge_scroll_width.description:
Width in pixels of the left/right edge-scroll bands. When the cursor
enters this band at the screen edge during a tile drag, the viewport
scrolls by one column (committed live, not deferred to release).

FloatingConfig.description:
Floating window configuration (`[floating]`).

The two size fields are optional explicit pixel sizes. When a field is
`None`, the daemon falls back to a built-in policy: 60% × 80% of the
monitor work area, capped so ultrawide / 4K monitors don't produce
absurdly large popups. The fallback constants live in
`src/daemon/dispatch.rs` (the sole consumer).

An explicit pixel value is always respected as-is — the cap applies only to
the fallback path.

[`always_on_top`](Self::always_on_top) is the niri-style **floating
layer**: floats stay above the tiled strip.

always_on_top.description:
Whether floating windows always sit **above the tiled windows**, as
in niri: every active float, and every window an explicit rule
ignores (dialogs and popups the user still wants to see), is kept in
the topmost band of the z-order (`HWND_TOPMOST`) while tiling is on,
so a dialog is never hidden behind a tile and never has to be hunted
for — even when a tiled window has the focus. A window leaves the
layer when it is tiled, minimized, hidden, put fullscreen, when
tiling is turned off and when the daemon stops; a window that was
already topmost on its own keeps that flag. Off by default (upstream
behaviour: a focused tile covers the floats). Live-reloadable. See
`daemon::top_layer`.

default_height.description: Explicit default float height in pixels. `None` → built-in fallback.

default_width.description: Explicit default float width in pixels. `None` → built-in fallback.

FocusConfig.description:
Focus reconciliation configuration.

`EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND` is a best-effort stream: under rapid window churn
(e.g. a browser tearing down tabs on close) the OS may settle the foreground
without emitting the final foreground event, leaving flow's internal focus
stranded on a stale window. To close that gap, the daemon periodically
reconciles its tracked focus against the authoritative `GetForegroundWindow()`
query on the main loop. (`docs/src/dev-guide/event-pipelines.md`)

foreground_sync_interval_ms.description:
Interval between foreground-reconciliation passes, in milliseconds.

Lower values catch drift sooner at the cost of more wakeups; the
per-pass work is a single `GetForegroundWindow()` read (~microseconds)
that no-ops when the tracked focus already matches reality. Tunable at
runtime via config hot-reload.

LoadoutConfig.description:
Loadout save/restore configuration.

Controls the file path used when saving or restoring workspace loadouts.

default_path.description:
File name (not a full path) used by `flow loadout save` and
`flow loadout restore`.

The daemon resolves this relative to the user's config directory
(`%USERPROFILE%\.config\flow\`). Defaults to `"loadout.json"`. It
must be a plain file name — no directories, no `..`, no drive —
which [`LoadoutConfig::validate`] enforces and config loading
rejects (`crate::loadout::validate_default_path`).

LoggingConfig.description:
Daemon log retention (`[logging]`).

The daemon writes one `logs/flowd-YYYY-MM-DD.log` per day under the
config directory and, at every start, deletes the ones older than
`keep_days` days (by the date in the file name). Those files record
every window the daemon met — executable, class and, at `debug` level,
the title — so they should not pile up forever by default.

keep_days.description:
How many days of daily log files to keep; older ones are deleted at
daemon start. `0` keeps every file forever (the upstream behaviour).

MinimizeRestore.description:
Strategy for restoring minimized tiling windows.

- `OriginalSlot` — put the window back where it was before minimize
- `RightOfFocused` — insert as a new column to the right of focused
- `AppendRight` — append as the rightmost column on the canvas

MinimizeRestoreStrategy.description:
Available minimize restore strategies.

See [`MinimizeRestore`] for the semantics of each variant.

oneOf.description: Put the window back where it was before minimize.
Insert as a new column to the right of focused.
Append as the rightmost column on the canvas.

NavigationConfig.description: Navigation behaviour at the edges of a strip.

edge_hop.description:
Whether `focus <dir>` and `move-window <dir>` at the end of a strip
hop to the monitor in that direction (niri behaviour). `false` makes
them stop at the edge; `focus-monitor` and `move-to-monitor` still
cross monitors.

Orientation.description: Which way a screen is turned, by its work area.

Padding.description:
Gap and margin configuration in pixels.

Gap is applied during the projection step (see [`projection`](crate::layout::projection)),
not stored inside window structs. This means [`ActualEntry`](crate::layout::ActualEntry) rects
are the **final HWND rects** — they can be passed directly to `SetWindowPos`.

# Uniform Gap Model

`window_gap` creates **uniform spacing** everywhere:

```text
Edge | window_gap | [Window 1] | window_gap | [Window 2] | window_gap | Edge
```

- `window_gap`: uniform gap between all elements (windows, screen edges)
- `up`: top screen margin (reserved space above tiling area)
- `down`: bottom screen margin (reserved space below tiling area, e.g., taskbar)

The slot-based canvas model ensures that expanding a column consumes the
inter-column gap so the layout always fills the screen.

```text
┌─────────────────── monitor work area ────────────────────┐
│ ↑ padding.up                                             │
│ ↑ window_gap                                             │
│ ┌──── window (HWND) ────┐   ┌──── window (HWND) ────┐    │
│ │                       │   │                       │    │
│ └───────────────────────┘   └───────────────────────┘    │
│ ↓ window_gap                                             │
│ ↓ padding.down                                           │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

down.description: Bottom screen margin — reserved space below the tiling area (e.g., taskbar).

up.description: Top screen margin — reserved space above the tiling area.

window_gap.description:
Uniform gap between all elements (windows and screen edges), in pixels.

This single value controls horizontal (inter-column), vertical (inter-row),
and edge-to-window spacing. Setting `window_gap = 16` means every gap
everywhere is 16 pixels.

ScreenMatch.description:
The `match` table of a `[[columns.screen]]` rule; every field given must
hold, and at least one must be given.

max_width_px.description: The work area must be at most this wide.

min_width_px.description: The work area must be at least this wide.

name.description:
The device name (`"DISPLAY2"`; the `\\.\` prefix is optional,
case-insensitive).

ScreenPresetRule.description:
One `[[columns.screen]]` rule: the presets a matching screen uses
instead of the top-level list.

default.description:
The preset such a screen starts on. Must be one of `presets`; when
omitted the first preset is the default.

match.description: Which screens the rule is for.

min_column_width_px.description:
A floor for this screen in place of the top-level
`min_column_width_px`, which is screen-blind.

presets.description:
Ordered presets for those screens; `flow dispatch width` walks this
list on them.

UpdateConfig.description:
Where `flow update` looks for something newer (`[update]`).

`flow update` is a **checker**: it asks the GitHub API how this build
relates to a branch or to the latest release and prints the answer; it
never downloads or replaces anything. Both keys are optional and fall
back to what the build script embedded (`crate::build_info`):

- `repo`: `"owner/name"` on github.com. Absent: parsed from the
  checkout's `origin` URL at build time when that is a github.com URL
  (https or ssh), else the upstream `CCpcalvin/flow-wm`.
- `branch`: the branch to compare the embedded commit against. Absent:
  the branch checked out at build time. An **empty string** (or no
  build branch to fall back to) switches to *release mode*: the latest
  release's tag is compared with the crate version instead.

branch.description:
Branch to compare against; `None` = the build's branch; `Some("")`
= compare against releases instead.

repo.description:
GitHub repository as `"owner/name"`; `None` = derived from the
build's `origin` URL, else upstream.
